newsitem.title: USA: Clinton refuses to engage on Jones case.
newsitem.headline: Clinton refuses to engage on Jones case.

text.p: President Clinton Wednesday refused to comment on a recent news report that he made sexual advances toward a former White House staffer who has since been subpoenaed in the Paula Jones case.

Clinton's personal attorney, Robert Bennett, has denied the allegation, published in a Newsweek article this weekend, calling it "a behind the scenes effort by the plaintiff's counsel to embarrass and humiliate the president by placing untrue stories in the press."
Bennett said former White House staffer Kathleen Willey had "no knowledge or information of any relevance regarding Paula Jones or her allegations."

Asked about the Newsweek report at a news conference, Clinton said, "Mr. Bennett and the person in question's lawyers gave the only relevant answers.... I don't really have anything to say to add to what Mr. Bennett already said about it."

Newsweek, in its current edition, which hit the newstands Monday, quoted Linda Tripp, a former executive assistant in the White House counsel's office, as saying that Willey had told her that Clinton had kissed and fondled her.

Tripp told the magazine she ran into Willey shortly after the encounter, which came during an Oval Office appointment with Clinton in November 1993, and Willey appeared "disheveled. Her face was red and her lipstick was off. She was flustered, happy and joyful."
Jones' lawyers have subpoenaed Willey in an effort to establish a pattern of improper sexual overtures by Clinton.
But Willey has said through her lawyers that she has no information relevant to the Jones case and would fight the subpoena.
Jones is suing the president, accusing him of sexually harassing her in a Little Rock hotel room while he was governor of Arkansas. Clinton has denied that the incident occurred.
